subject.title: Feature Request: config:pre-apply hook for validating config changes

question: Should OpenClaw add a synchronous plugin/API config-write veto hook, and what ordering, trust, redaction, timeout, recursion, and failure semantics should it have across RPC and shared config mutation paths?
rationale: Source inspection proves the missing seam, but the permanent API shape changes plugin trust, config persistence, auth/provider safety, and gateway availability behavior that require maintainer intent.

options.title: Design guarded config-write hook
options.body: Add a narrow documented pre-persistence hook or config mutation contract covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit security semantics.

options.title: Limit to built-in validation
options.body: Keep config validation and agent-write allowlists in core only, and document external validators as optional helpers that cannot enforce mandatory pre-apply policy.

options.title: Fold into broader preflight RFC
options.body: Defer the hook until the broader config validation/preflight direction chooses one shared validation contract and failure policy.

recommendation.title: Design guarded config-write hook
recommendation.body: Add a narrow documented pre-persistence hook or config mutation contract covering `config.set`, `config.patch`, `config.apply`, and shared mutation helpers with explicit security semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already framed this issue as an unresolved config validation/mutation product boundary and has recent history on the relevant config and hook surfaces.
